articles.title: The Strangest Animal Found in Each State
articles.summary: Whether they act weird, sound weird or seem like something out of a sci-fi novel, these animals are very strange indeed
articles.body:
The Red Hills salamander is an endangered species due to habitat loss caused by logging and deforestation.

The Ice worm can liquefy and die if exposed to temperatures above 40 degrees Fahrenheit.

The Javelina is distinguished from wild pigs by its scent gland in the rump used for marking territory and identification.

This official state amphibian is a long, lean, mean burrowing machine. Much larger than its other lungless salamander peers at 11 inches, the Red Hills salamander breathes through its moist skin. It's on the U.S. Fish & Wildlife endangered species list because much of its 60,000 acres of suitable habitat (i.e., the steep slopes and moist ravines of hardwood forests) are threatened by logging and deforestation.

This relative of common earthworms and leeches makes its home inside glaciers and adjacent snowfields, moving through densely packed ice crystals with ease thanks to small bristles on the outside of its body. Its Latin name, Solifugus , meaning sun avoider, is basically a warning to the annelid, which thrives best at 32 degrees Fahrenheit. According to the Alaska Centers public lands guide, when heated to 40 degrees, an ice worm's insides liquefy until it literally melts to death. Ouch!

Javelinas, also known as a collared peccary, are often confused for wild pigs thanks to their stumpy legs, porcine-like snouts and tendency to communicate in snorts. But according to the Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, these "new world" herbivores/frugivores (fruit eaters) are distinguished from their "old world" animal lookalikes by numerous physical features, including a scent gland in their rump that they rub on rocks and stumps to mark their territory and on one another for identification. Pigs, on the other hand, lack scent glands.

These endangered and nearly translucent cave dwellers live most or all of their lives in total darkness. But they're blind because they lack eyes altogether and therefore use sense organs to detect movement in the water and find food. Very little is known about their reproductive habits, but the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service and the Missouri Department of Conservation suspect that spring floods get them in the mood for making whoopee.

The sex life of these gooey, yellow mollusks is even more bizarre than their coloring or the fact that they inch down from high tree branches on thin strands of slime in much the same way as spiders utilize their webbing. For starters, according to Field Guide to the Slug by David George Gordon, they are hermaphrodites. Two, a slug penis, which emerges from its head, can be as long as its entire body. That makes for some of the largest male genitalia of any species in proportion to its overall size. Three, reproductive sessions last hours and sometimes end in apophallation, which is when a banana slug gnaws off and eats its partner's privates. They do not grow back.

Although these low fast fliers have poor eyesight themselves, they are quite the spectacle to watch during the spring breeding season. Defenders of Wildlife explains that males develop white chest feathers and specialized head plumage, and that is just the beginning of their fascinating mating ritual. At dawn or dusk, birds in the mood for love assemble on leks—ancestral strutting grounds returned to annually that can be as far as 50 miles from their winter habitats—and strut, fan their tail feathers and puff their chests until bright yellow air sacs are revealed and hens are smitten.

Star-nosed moles, according to National Geographic , eat faster than any other mammal on earth. They decide if something is edible in eight milliseconds and devour their meal (mostly bugs) in less than two-tenths of a second. They owe part of their unusual animal superpower to the extremely efficient operation of their nervous system, and part to their hideous "noses." The star, which contains 100,000 nerve fibers in a space smaller than your fingertip, is the most sensitive touch organ in any mammal. They are also the only mammal known to smell underwater, and again they have their grotesque snouts to thank. Moles blow bubbles into the water and then re-inhale them to catch a whiff of potential prey.

These birds may be labeled "common," but their foraging techniques are anything but. Grackles follow plows to catch invertebrates and mice, snatch leeches from the legs of turtles, raid nests and steal worms from other birds, wade in shallow water to fish and use the hard keel on the inside of their upper mandible to saw open acorns. They also practice the strange habit of anting, in which they get low to the ground, wings spread, and let ants crawl all over them. It is postulated that the formic acid deposited by the insects gets rid of parasites. When they can't find ants, grackles have been known to use walnut juice, marigolds, lemons, limes and mothballs to achieve the same results.

Although manatees are born underwater and never go ashore in their lives, the mammals with egg-shaped heads are related to elephants, not dolphins or whales, according to National Geographic . The blubbery, gentle giants known as sea cows congregate near Florida power plant discharge pipes because the water is warmer there. Smithsonian.com reports that they eat for almost half the day, consuming 10% of their 1,200-pound body weight in plants.

At first glance, it is easy to confuse the one-toed amphiuma for a water snake or an eel. In fact, one of its common names is the ditch eel. But according to the Wildlife Resources Division of Georgia's Department of Natural Resources, it is a very rare elongated salamander with two pairs of tiny seemingly useless limbs (common to salamanders), with a single toe on each (unique to this species). It lacks external gills, and although it has gill slits, it breathes by periodically lifting its nose out of the mud or water.

Hawaii's tourism boards would have people believe there are no snakes in paradise. And while there are not any that are indigenous to the 50th state, the claim is technically a fib. Let us be the first to introduce you to the blind snake, the world's tiniest snake. Most likely spotted on Hawaii Island and Kauai, this earthworm lookalike was introduced to the state in the 1980s, likely in potting soil from the Philippines. They have managed to survive on the islands because they are the only known parthenogenic snakes, meaning their unfertilized eggs hatch into new female clones. (Geckos also utilize this adaptation.) And because they eat termites and ants, which are also non-native, they do not have any measurable effects on the ecosystem.

Weight-watchers should be jealous of the second-smallest mammal in the world, because despite consuming as much as three times its body weight every day and eating every three to four hours to maintain body heat, a pygmy shrew usually weighs less than an ounce and is 2 inches long. For them, their extraordinarily high metabolism is more of a curse, given that it means they have to be on a constant hunt for food and can't sleep for more than a few minutes at a time. Shrews swim, use the tunnels and nests of other animals, and burrow through snow in pursuit of the next meal. To compensate for a short food supply in winter, they may lose up to 40% of their body weight, which basically makes them a bag of bones and organs.

Spiders are generally creepy as a species, but a venomous spider that can grow slightly wider than a human adult's palm and submerge itself for more than 30 minutes to fish for small aquatic dwellers like tadpoles is next-level sinister. The hairs on a fishing spider's body trap air bubbles, which they use to breathe underwater while stalking their next meal. While down there, they also scope out the area above them because they can simultaneously eat insects skittering around and just above the water's surface. Oh, and as part of the nursery-web family, a female lays eggs on a silken mat, which she wraps into a ball and then carries around in her jaws until she finds an ideal spot for them to hatch. It is attached to an elaborate web until hundreds of spiderlings emerge all at once and then disperse on their own silky threads to start fresh lives of hunting and haunting your nightmares.

These 2-foot-long and flattened aquatic salamanders with a devilish name once roamed nearly all of the Ohio River tributaries, but numbers are dwindling at a startling rate. Fewer than 300 remain in the state, all in the Blue River, according to The Nature Conservancy, thanks to degrading water quality, loss of habitat, accidental fishing and fatal human interactions. A rumor even puts them on plates at a Harrison County fish fry in the 1970s. It would be a shame to lose what Popular Mechanics calls "a living fossil" because relatives of the gentle mud puppy show very little external evolution as far back as 160 million years.

No, they don't come from France , but these insects with pointy, pinched conical faces do consume mass quantities of grasses and corn crops. They have antennae longer than their bodies, strong jaws that can injure humans, and very long and powerful hind legs for jumping. Females have sword-like ovipositors to lay fertilized eggs inside plant tissue. According to InsectIdentification.org, they can be found by listening for their chirpy songs.

If an animal version of the Academy Awards existed, the hognose snake would be the reptilian Meryl Streep, thanks to its convincing death scenes. (Although it can't help but turn up its nose at fame.) When a hognose feels threatened, Reptiles Magazine explains, it hisses, flattens its neck, raises its head like a cobra and feigns strikes. If that fails to scare away its enemy, it will roll onto its back and play dead. It emits a stinky musk, poops and lets its tongue hang out, sometimes even excreting blood droplets. If flipped upright while in this state, it will roll over again and continue the charade.

Scorpion flies look Frankenstein-ed together. According to The Wildlife Trusts, they have a tail that looks like the stinger of a scorpion, although they don't sting and it is not a tail at all. It's actually the male's clasper, which is used in courtship. Mating can be dangerous for males, as the females have been known to kill their lovers. To dissuade her from post-mating murder, these garden/wood dwellers, which have never met a stinging nettle bush they didn't like, will offer a dead insect or a wad of saliva. Its head contains a long beak used to feed.

The spoonbill is hard to miss, thanks to its millennial-pink feathers. But it's the long, speckled proboscis that leaves a lasting impression. Especially if you get to see one swinging it side to side to push away the muck in mudflats, tide pools, mangrove keys and coastal marshes while on the prowl for crustaceans, snails and various other residents of shallow waters. According to the Audubon Field Guide , they also use that beak as foreplay. Males and females first interact aggressively then huddle close, present twigs to each other and wildly cross and clasp bills. For an unknown reason, the entire flock will suddenly fly up and circle the breeding area at the beginning of the season. They are no deadbeat dads either. They use the bill to gather materials to construct the nest, should mating be successful, and eventually help feed their young.

An Oxford University study revealed that tardigrades, eight-legged microscopic critters with a sucker-like pharynx on their face, could outlive humans by 10 billion years because the sturdy water bears can survive extreme conditions, including dehydration, freezing, autoclaving, exposure to the vacuum of space and irradiation, by using cryptobiosis to shut down their metabolism. They live in water and on lichen and moss in most countries and states, including Maine.

This massive semi-aquatic rodent was introduced to America back in 1899 to kickstart a fur-farm industry. When the market collapsed in the 1940s, U.S. Fish & Wildlife reports that thousands were released into the wild and have been reportedly seen in 40 states. Nutria spend their days demolishing vegetation and roots, damaging ditches and levies by burrowing, reproducing like wildfire (females can breed 48 hours after giving birth) and frightening musophobes (people afraid of rats) with their beaver-like looks. Their front legs are smaller than their rear ones, giving them a hunchback appearance. They have large yellow-orange front teeth, heavy scaly tails covered in wiry hairs and facial features set high on their heads. Then there's the vestigial toe dangling unconnected to the webbing that holds the other toes together. It does not show up in their animal tracks . Female teats are also on the side of the body instead of the chest.

This is the kind of repugnant mug you can't un-see. The devil is the green, orange and black caterpillar stage of the royal walnut/regal moth. But its looks and name are a ruse, as the horns don't even sting. Devils are also easily handled by humans. They molt five times, becoming bright green on the fifth round. Before pupation, a larva expels its guts and changes color to turquoise before heading underground. When they emerge as moths, they have severely reduced mouths so they do not feed and can only live for about a week.

Don't go insulting the largest turtles in North America, because the snapping turtle will clap back. Equipped with not only a ferocious albeit toothless mouth, they have a growth on the tip of their tongues that looks like a wiggly worm, reports the University of Michigan's Bio Kids website. While buried in the mud or hidden by vegetation, turtles use the "worm" to lure fish into their jaws and eventually bellies. Some scientists believe they have developed such an aggressive personality because, unlike most of their relatives, they cannot retract their limbs or head into their shells for protection. These curmudgeonly turtles are solitary, with social interactions limited to fighting with other males. To pick up a mate, turtles face each other and communicate with leg movements.

These frogs don't look bizarre, but they have developed a pretty unique adaptation that comes in handy in a state with famously brutal winters. The Twin Cities Pioneer Press details the tree frog's ability to freeze partially during the winter. It produces large amounts of glycerol to protect its body during the freezing process, but its heart, breathing and other vital functions can stop. Once it thaws, the frog will reanimate.

These behemoth fish, which can grow to more than 8 feet long, look like they belong in a natural history museum, because alligator gars retain many of their Cretaceous ancestors' primitive features, including the ability to breath air, a body covered by sharp rigid scales, very sharp teeth and much stronger bites than most fish you'll find lurking in lakes in many Southern states. Popular Mechanics also says they have a similar digestive system to sharks.

It's hard not to get the heebie-jeebies when looking at a photo of this freaky animal , a giant desert centipede, the largest centipede in North America, and its 21 or 23 pairs of yellow legs, fangs, red head and greenish-black body. The bright coloration is aposematic, meaning it should act as a warning to stay away. The centipede hunts invertebrates and small vertebrates including rodents and reptiles, sometimes reaching into the air to grab flying bugs, and uses its cell-rupturing, membrane-compromising venom to subdue its future food. It can also pinch with its last pair of legs to bring the pain, according to the Missouri Department of Conservation.

Often confused for an antelope, pronghorns, with their distinctive backward-curving horns, belong to a family of mammals all their own. After the cheetah, they are the second fastest land mammal in the world, running more than 53 miles an hour, according to National Geographic— even babies can outrun humans within a few days of being born. They can also go the distance if they cut down to half that speed. But despite their long legs and ability to achieve a running start, they rarely jump fences, instead choosing to go underneath them. The pronghorn warning system is also guaranteed to make young children giggle: When frightened, the hairs on their behinds raises into a white patch that can be seen for miles.

Of the 20 species of little-armored ones (the name's Spanish translation), only the nine-banded armadillo—which, despite the name, can actually have anywhere from 7 to 11 bands—is found in the United States. Once relegated to southeastern states, their range is continually expanding northward, and now the bizarre beasts with ossified dermal scutes, keratinized epidermal scales, long sticky tongues and hairy undersides are often spotted in the Cornhusker State . The insectivore cannot curl into a ball and roll away from danger, contrary to popular belief. (Only two types of armadillos can ball up, according to The National Wildlife Federation.) But it can jump 3 to 4 feet in the air, float across rivers by inflating its intestines, hold its breath for six minutes while running across riverbeds and quickly dig a snug trench to lodge itself in when in danger.

Also known as a jewel spider, it belongs to a subset of spiders called angulates, which can be identified by the presence of two pronounced bumps on the top of its abdomen. Those bumps form the ears of the feline face found on this eight-legged creepy crawler. Sitting with its head toward the ground is this spider's preferred stance, so most of the time the kitty appears upside down. But rest easy, cat ladies have nothing to fear from this harmless-to-humans fellow.

The buffalo treehopper is a tiny green plant jumper that earned its name because the pest appears to have horns and a tail that resemble those of a bison. But the tail is actually just the pointy end of the ridge on its back, and the horns are the colored protuberances that come out of the widest part of its head.

Every 13 or 17 years, these red-eyed freaks of nature emerge from living underground, where they subsist on tree-root fluids, through chimneys/turrets they build out of mud, then immediately shed their skin. Harmless cicadas ascend synchronously in tremendous numbers in spring, often after a light rain. Males band together as a chorus to sing to potential mates, and within a couple of months, eggs are laid and the adults disappear once again.

These guys make the list simply because New Mexico is a strange place to find such a big wild herd. As their other name implies, the African oryx hail from another continent. According to Popular Mechanics , the gemsbok made their way out of Africa in 1969 when a group of 95 was transplanted from the savannahs of Southern Africa to the White Sands Missile Range and the surrounding area of New Mexico, to give local hunters a big-game target. That group thrived, thanks to a lack of natural predators, and now number more than 3,000. The beasts of the Southern Africa wild, which stand as tall as the roof of a car on average, are often seen in White Sands National Monument.

The Seneca Army Depot, a former wildlife sanctuary and military museum built on a 7,000-acre former munitions and nuclear bomb storage facility in the Finger Lakes region, was home to the world's largest herd of white deer. These ghost deer, a natural variation of the white-tailed species caused by a recessive gene, are not albinos. They are leucistic and therefore lack all pigmentation in their hair, but they have normal noses and brown eyes. According to the depot's nonprofit organization's website, limited predators and controlled hunting on the defunct base allowed numbers to increase for more than 60 years.

Abundant in the eastern part of the state, these guys are often mistaken for snakes. But glass lizards are actually (usually) legless lizards because of their head shape, movable eyelids and external ear openings. Some have retained small, stubby and useless vestigial legs. The name refers to the tendency of their tails to easily break into several pieces like glass when they drop them to avoid being captured or eaten. It can take years for the tail to grow back, and it is almost always smaller than its predecessor.

A unique fur pattern makes these skunks stand out in the crowd of sprayers. But the name is a bit of a misnomer, as they have only one spot—on the forehead. They are, however, missing that traditional center white stripe and look more like a weasel. In many other ways, these skunks are like your average backyard intruder, especially when it comes to their defense mechanisms. First comes the warning. There's front feet stomping, tail raising, hissing and sometimes a handstand-like position that puts their shooter (aka their tush) in the air. If that doesn't work, two glands on the sides of the anus will release odorous oil through nipples.

They vaaaant to suck your blood. Well, maybe not your blood, per se, but these aquatic vampires attach jawless disc-shaped mouths to fish in streams and rivers and feast on their blood. According to Ohio's Division of Wildlife, seven species including the non-native sea lamprey are found in Buckeye State waters. Sea lampreys also use their gnarly mouths to suction cup and move stones to form a breeding pit. Pits are made and used by the whole community of parasites.

If you are lucky enough to catch a glimpse of these timid and tiny (usually only a pound or two, and 24 inches in length) nocturnal animals, it's likely you'll mistake them for a really pretty house cat, an escaped zoo lemur thanks to oversized eyes and a long ringed tail of 14 to 16 black-and-white stripes, or a fox because of their pointy muzzle and whiskers. But they are relatives of coatis and raccoons. They are great climbers, and according to the Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, having the ability to rotate their back paws 180 degrees allows them to ascend walls, trees, cliffs and even cacti. Their ears have also adapted to move independently of each other, so ringtails can listen to what's happening in front of and behind them simultaneously.

Generally found in the eastern half of the state and occasionally west of the Cascade Mountains, according to OregonLive.com, porcupines are better left alone. Covered in up to 30,000 sharp, barbed quills they use for defense, these slow rodents are shown in studies to be intelligent, to be able to learn and to have long memories, especially of mistreatment, according to National Geographic . If rattling their quills doesn't scare off predators, they will ram backward into them, as the quills cannot be shot out of the body. They do, however, grow back over time. Porcupines don't ask for trouble, and they are herbivores but have been seen chewing on animal bones to sharpen their teeth and intake minerals like salt and calcium to stay healthy.

Don't call it a comeback. The paddlefish has been here for years—since the Paleozoic era (300 to 400 million years ago), to be precise. Fossil evidence of this long-snouted filter-feeding fish is millions of years old. The paddle, which is longer than the rest of its head and flat on the top and bottom, might be a touch organ or it may help stabilize the fish when its jaw is extended. Strangely, young paddlefish do not have the trademark rostrum. They also have teeth, while the adult versions, which can weigh more than 200 pounds, do not.

National Geographic warns about the perils of ignoring this aggressive, invasive fish with reptilian coloring, razor-sharp teeth that can tear human flesh, a ravenous appetite and an ability to be amphibious. That's right, these bad boys can not only survive on land for three days using a primitive lung above their gills, they can walk on it by rhythmically swinging their muscular bodies and fins back and forth. Also a problem: Snakeheads reach sexual maturity by two or three, mate up to five times a year and can release 15,000 eggs at once.

Sheepshead fish, which can be found in waters from Massachusetts to Brazil, look like a genetic experiment gone wrong, thanks to their human teeth. A Scientific American blog post explains that fully grown convict fish—a nickname inspired by the distinctive black bars running down their silvery bodies—have well-defined incisors at the front of their jaw, multiple rows of molars and strong grinders at the back. This unique, humanlike combination of choppers allows them to bite into armored prey like clams, crabs and barnacles. Talk about a killer smile.

These guys are pretty darn cute, but they are also cutthroat hunters with huge appetites, according to World Atlas. Their wee bodies, usually 5 to 7 inches in length with an inch-long tail, transform when on the hunt for voles and mice. They can narrow their bodies to follow prey into a tiny burrow or hole the size of a wedding ring. Their coats also change color seasonally—brown in summer and white to match the winter snow—to provide better camouflage . Once they find a target, they swiftly latch onto the back of its head and bite through its skull with their very sharp teeth.

The Tennessee cave salamander, a slimy pale pink creature with a pale belly and bright red feathery external gills, was designated the state amphibian in 1995. Now on the threatened list, they live in streams found inside caves and sinkholes, according to Tennessee Watchable Wildlife .

Despite its name, the jaguarundi's closet relative is the mountain lion. It does not share either the jaguar or mountain lion's ferocious reputation, mostly because this rodent hunter is only 30 inches from nose to tail. They are also born with spots like a leopard but lose them with age. The mini cat that looks more like a weasel than a cougar is common in Central and South America, where it was used as a Pied Piper on small village rat populations, but the Gulf Coast of the Lone Star State is the only place they are found in the U.S., according to Big Cat Rescue. The often solitary animals occasionally forage and travel in pairs, communicating with 13 distinct recorded vocalizations.

These black and ivory, pimply relatives of Komodo dragons have small hidden beady eyes and look like they are missing lips. Fortunately for humans, they spend 95% of their time underground and lumber around slowly when they do emerge, because they are incredibly venomous. When they bite, poison secreted by their salivary glands is propelled through their teeth by chewing and capillary action into their victim. Pioneers used to believe their breath was toxic, but in an ironic twist of fate, peptides found in their venom have been shown to inhibit lung cancer growth and treat diabetes, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill research.

These mink-like, housecat-size omnivores were long considered extirpated from the boreal forests of the Green Mountain State, despite an attempt to reintroduce them from 1989 and 1991. But Vermont's Department of Fish and Wildlife started reporting new sightings of the shy guys in 2014. They average 21 to 26 inches long, with a third of that length coming from their bushy tails. As agile climbers, they spend lots of time in trees, hunting for squirrels and chipmunks, nesting and birthing their annual litters. The marten can rotate its hind legs to descend trees headfirst.

This is the kind of insect nightmares are made of—narrow heads, wide abdomens that generally flare upward, "butts" that tip into the air, black bodies with bright red markings and a terrifying fang that can inflict an intense bite on humans. They earned their names because they move nimbly and rapidly when on the hunt. Powerful front legs pin down insects, while a strong beak emerges from its hiding place under the head and repeatedly stabs it like a serial killer. Once the insect is dead, it sucks out the insides.

The largest intertidal and biggest burrowing clam in the world (as well as one of the longest-living animals) makes its home in the chilly coastal substrates and silts of the Pacific Northwest and British Columbia . The valves stay open in adult geoducks because the body and siphons are too large to retract. This defining feature inspired the Chinese to refer to them as elephant trunk clams. It can stretch its neck 24 inches from its body. Geoducks, considered a delicacy in culinary circles, position themselves about 3 feet deep in the sand and then hang there for 100 years.

Looks can kill in the case of these wooly slugs. It may look furry and soft, but the long brown silky hairs of the puss caterpillar hide hollow poisonous spines that can cause intense pain, swelling, itchy rash, anxiety, fever, muscle cramps, swollen glands and vomiting, according to the University of Michigan. This makes them the most poisonous caterpillars in the United States.

Warning: You might never look at lakes in the same way again after reading about this globular creature that Popular Mechanics reports has been sighted numerous times in the fresh waters of America's Dairyland, despite being indigenous to China. But you can exhale, as the 1-inch Craspedacusta sowerbii , a freshwater jellyfish or hydra relative, has stingers far too small to pierce human skin. If you want to witness them, the best time is August or September in calm, shallow waters, although inexplicably, their numbers vary wildly from season to season.

No, Hugh Jackman doesn't finish out the list. We're talking about the largest terrestrial member of the Mustelid family, with its broad head, beady eyes and minor underbite. These beasts are survivors adapted to take on polar vortexes with no need to hibernate, thanks to their dark oily fur that withstands frost. Wide feet act like natural snowshoes, and upper molars at the backs of their mouths are rotated 90 degrees to allow them to rip meat from frozen-solid carrion. They also have the energy to travel some 15 miles a day in search of food, and females practice embryonic diapause, a delayed implantation of the embryo to the uterus months after breeding. Interestingly, when their bundles of joy finally make an appearance, they are pure white.

articles.summary: Projeto desenvolvido por estudantes do 8º termo aproxima os futuros engenheiros de desafios presentes nos setores industrial e automotivo
articles.body:
Engenharia Mecânica do UNIFEB transforma teoria em prática com trocadores — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação Unifeb

Estudantes do 8º termo de Engenharia Mecânica do UNIFEB (Centro Universitário da Fundação Educacional de Barretos) estão colocando em prática conhecimentos adquiridos em sala de aula por meio de um projeto de construção de um trocador de calor do tipo casco e tubo, desenvolvido integralmente pelos próprios alunos. A iniciativa tem como objetivo consolidar os conceitos teóricos abordados na disciplina de Transferência de Calor, proporcionando uma experiência completa de desenvolvimento de engenharia.

Segundo o Prof. Me. Vicente de Paulo Gonçalves Junior, coordenador do curso de Engenharia Mecânica do UNIFEB, o projeto envolve a concepção e fabricação do equipamento “do zero”. O aparato experimental foi desenvolvido para promover a troca térmica entre dois fluxos de água em contracorrente, ou seja, em sentidos opostos, fazendo com que os fluidos circulem por vias distintas e sem contato direto.

Esse tipo de equipamento possui ampla aplicação nos setores industrial e automotivo, o que permite aos estudantes compreenderem, na prática, o funcionamento de uma tecnologia presente no mercado profissional. O projeto também incorporou conhecimentos de instrumentação e automação, com a utilização de termopares acoplados a um display para a visualização das temperaturas em tempo real.

Para o professor Vicente, os resultados alcançados podem ser analisados sob duas perspectivas: pedagógica e experimental.

“Sob a perspectiva pedagógica, os estudantes consolidaram o aprendizado ao aplicar de forma direta os conceitos teóricos de otimização em processos de transferência de calor”, explica.

Na prática, os estudantes tiveram contato com todas as etapas do desenvolvimento de um equipamento de engenharia.

“Os alunos vivenciaram o ciclo completo de desenvolvimento de engenharia, construindo o trocador de calor desde a sua concepção inicial”, destaca o coordenador.

O trabalho envolveu ainda o domínio de processos de fabricação, como soldagem e usinagem, além da integração de sistemas de instrumentação e automação. Ao final, todos os grupos alcançaram resultados considerados altamente satisfatórios, comprovando a funcionalidade e a eficiência operacional dos dispositivos construídos.

APRENDIZADO CONECTADO À REALIDADE PROFISSIONAL

A experiência prática é considerada pelo coordenador um componente importante na formação dos futuros engenheiros.

“A inserção de projetos práticos na formação acadêmica é fundamental, pois permite ao estudante visualizar, de forma integral, os fenômenos físicos estudados em sala de aula”, afirma.

No caso da Transferência de Calor, a aplicação prática possibilita aos alunos compreenderem como características geométricas e variáveis dinâmicas interferem diretamente na eficiência energética de um sistema.

De acordo com Vicente, esse conhecimento representa um diferencial importante para a carreira.

“O domínio dessa temática é crucial, visto que a otimização de processos e a sustentabilidade energética são competências altamente requisitadas pelas empresas modernas na contratação de profissionais de engenharia”, ressalta.

O projeto também dialoga diretamente com as demandas atuais do mercado de trabalho. Para o coordenador, a Engenharia Mecânica permanece em um cenário favorável devido à busca constante das empresas por soluções capazes de aumentar a eficiência operacional e, ao mesmo tempo, reduzir o consumo de energia.

“Atualmente, a eficiência energética é um pilar estratégico para grandes empresas que visam reduzir custos e mitigar impactos ambientais”, destaca.

Nesse contexto, o engenheiro mecânico exerce papel fundamental ao reunir competências técnicas para projetar, simular e implementar melhorias contínuas, transformando objetivos corporativos em resultados práticos.

AUTONOMIA PARA “ENGENHEIRAR” DESDE A GRADUAÇÃO

A experiência integra a proposta pedagógica adotada nos cursos de Engenharia do UNIFEB, que busca complementar a formação acadêmica por meio de atividades práticas diretamente relacionadas aos Projetos Integradores.

Nesse modelo, o professor responsável pela disciplina atua como facilitador do processo de aprendizagem, estimulando a autonomia dos estudantes para que possam aplicar os conhecimentos adquiridos na resolução de problemas concretos.

Para o coordenador, essa abordagem contribui para desenvolver competências que ultrapassam o conhecimento técnico, estimulando pensamento crítico, tomada de decisões e inovação desde a formação acadêmica.

“Assim, a construção dos trocadores de calor representa mais do que a aplicação de conceitos de Transferência de Calor: é uma oportunidade para que os estudantes experimentem, na prática, as diferentes etapas que fazem parte da atuação de um engenheiro mecânico, aproximando a formação universitária dos desafios encontrados no mercado profissional”, finaliza Vicente.

articles.title: Gabriel Azevedo propõe criação de corredores ferroviários em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Gabriel tem 40 anos, é advogado, professor universitário e jornalista. Na política, foi vereador e presidente da Câmara Municipal de Belo Horizonte.
articles.summary: Gabriel tem 38 anos, é advogado, professor universitário e jornalista. Na política, foi vereador e presidente da Câmara Municipal de Belo Horizonte.
articles.body:
Gabriel Azevedo participou de entrevista no Inter 1 — Foto: Reprodução/Inter TV

O candidato ao Governo de Minas Gabriel Azevedo (MDB) disse, em entrevista à Inter TV nesta quinta-feira (3), que pretende criar corredores ferroviários no estado, valorizar a educação e adotar medidas para o enfrentamento da seca. Ele também afirmou que o combate ao feminicídio será uma das prioridades no seu governo.

Gabriel tem 40 anos, é advogado, professor universitário e jornalista. Na política, foi vereador e presidente da Câmara Municipal de Belo Horizonte.

Durante a entrevista, o candidato apresentou propostas para diversas áreas e destacou a criação de ferrovias que vão ligar diferentes regiões de Minas Gerais. Ele afirmou que pretende implantar 15 corredores ferroviários no estado. Entre as propostas está a criação de uma linha ligando Corinto, Montes Claros , Janaúba e Caetité, na Bahia.

A proposta também prevê uma ligação ferroviária entre Bocaiuva, Montes Claros e Janaúba, com possibilidade de transporte de passageiros. O candidato ainda citou a criação de corredores que atendam o Noroeste de Minas, o Vale do Jequitinhonha e o Vale do Mucuri.

Segundo o candidato, as ferrovias seriam viabilizadas com recursos do Governo Federal.

“No Governo Federal, há cerca de R$ 20 bilhões parados esperando projetos pra gente fazer ferrovia. A obra não vai começar e terminar em quatro anos, e é isso que Minas Gerais está precisando: político que não queira ficar colocando plaquinha”.

De acordo com Gabriel, a ampliação da malha ferroviária pode reduzir os custos do transporte de fertilizantes e melhorar o escoamento da produção.

Ao falar sobre a seca, o candidato disse que pretende investir em segurança hídrica regional e integrar a gestão das bacias hidrográficas.

Entre as medidas citadas estão a proteção de nascentes, o apoio à construção de barragens, o fortalecimento dos órgãos responsáveis pela gestão dos recursos hídricos e investimentos em saneamento rural.

Gabriel também afirmou que pretende ampliar o tratamento de esgoto para reduzir a poluição dos rios e disse que a seca não pode ser usada como “indústria de voto”.

Na área da educação, o candidato afirmou que pretende priorizar a aprendizagem e a valorização dos professores.

Gabriel criticou a aprovação de estudantes que não adquiriram os conhecimentos necessários durante o ano letivo. Segundo o candidato, a ideia é acompanhar o desenvolvimento dos alunos e oferecer reforço àqueles que apresentarem dificuldades.

Ele também citou parcerias com instituições como a Unimontes, a UFMG e o IFNMG para aprimorar a formação e a didática dos professores, além de defender a valorização salarial da categoria.

“Aqui está um professor que valoriza o professor. Vamos garantir a aprendizagem no tempo certo. [...] Comigo é uma educação que tem aprendizagem”.

Gabriel Azevedo também disse que pretende reduzir os casos de feminicídio no estado e ampliar a rede de acolhimento às mulheres vítimas de violência.

Entre as medidas defendidas estão a integração das forças de segurança, o uso de inteligência no combate aos crimes e o fortalecimento do atendimento especializado às vítimas.

“Temos uma prioridade no nosso plano de governo: feminicídio zero, nenhuma mulher pode morrer por ser mulher. [...] Nosso compromisso é que nenhuma mulher morra por ser mulher e, mais do que isso, que exista uma rede de acolhimento e recomeço”.

articles.title: Tentativa de assalto em Sobral: casal reage e rende suspeito | G1
articles.standfirst: Outro suspeito conseguiu fugir correndo e abandonou uma moto no local.
articles.summary: Após tentativa de assalto em Sobral, uma mulher derrubou o criminoso e o companheiro o imobilizou até a chegada da Guarda Municipal, enquanto o segundo suspeito fugiu.
articles.body:
Um casal reagiu a uma tentativa de assalto e rendeu um dos suspeitos durante uma abordagem na Rua Coronel Sabino Guimarães, no Bairro Padre Ibiapina, em Sobral , no interior do Ceará. O caso ocorreu na oite da última terça-feira (1º) e foi registrado por uma câmera de segurança.

O motociclista vítima da ação estava parado em frente uma residência, aguardando a mulher que estava saindo de casa. Enquanto o homem esperava, dois suspeitos em outra moto se aproximaram e tentaram rendê-lo.

Ao ver a cena, a mulher empurrou um dos suspeitos , fazendo ele se desequilibrar e derrubar a moto usada no crime. O homem saiu correndo e abandonou o veículo no local. Já o comparsa, foi atingido por murros e chutes desferidos pelo motociclista e terminou rendido pelo casal.

Suspeito é rendido por casal e preso pela Guarda Municipal durante tentativa de assalto em Sobral. — Foto: Reprodução

A Guarda Municipal foi acionada e conduziu o suspeito para a Delegacia de Sobral. A moto abandonada pelos criminosos também foi apresentada na unidade policial.

Durante a ocorrência, foi identificado que a moto usada pelo suspeitos apresentava pendências administrativas. Com isso, o veículo foi encaminhado ao pátio do Detran.

articles.title: Irã promete vingança após ataque a casamento atribuído aos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataque que atingiu uma festa de casamento deixou quatro mortos no sul do Irã; Washington nega ter bombardeado civis.
articles.summary: Ataque que atingiu uma festa de casamento deixou quatro mortos no sul do Irã; Washington nega ter bombardeado civis.
articles.body:
O comandante da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã , Ahmad Vahidi , prometeu nesta quinta-feira (3) vingar as quatro pessoas mortas em uma cerimônia de casamento no sul do país. Teerã atribui o ataque aos Estados Unidos .

"O sangue puro desses mártires oprimidos (...) não ficará sem resposta e certamente será vingado", afirmou Vahidi em comunicado divulgado pela televisão estatal iraniana.

O ataque aconteceu na última terça-feira (1°), segundo autoridades iranianas e o Crescente Vermelho. Entre as vítimas, estaria uma criança de 4 anos.

O episódio ocorreu em meio à escalada do confronto entre os dois países . No mesmo dia, forças americanas realizaram novos ataques contra posições ligadas à Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica. Washington afirmou que as ações foram uma resposta a supostas tentativas iranianas de atacar navios comerciais no Estreito de Ormuz e militares americanos na região.

Após o ataque ao casamento, o governo iraniano condenou a ação e prometeu retaliação. O porta-voz da chancelaria, Esmaeil Baqaei , afirmou que o país responderia aos Estados Unidos e classificou como perigosa qualquer tentativa de normalizar bombardeios contra áreas civis.

Em seguida, o Irã anunciou ataques com drones e mísseis contra alvos americanos na região . Autoridades iranianas disseram que a ofensiva fazia parte da resposta à campanha militar dos EUA contra o país.

A retórica iraniana aumentou nos dias seguintes. Baqaei classificou o caso como um "crime de guerra", enquanto outras autoridades acusaram os Estados Unidos de terem atacado civis deliberadamente durante a celebração do casamento.

articles.title: Serra Madre é o seu melhor jeito de conhecer maravilhas de Rio Quente | G1
articles.standfirst: Maior rio de águas termais do mundo, Serra de Caldas e parque aquático de 55 mil m² estão no mesmo raio de poucos minutos: a casa de férias entra como base fixa do roteiro.
articles.summary: Maior rio de águas termais do mundo, Serra de Caldas e parque aquático de 55 mil m² estão no mesmo raio de poucos minutos: a casa de férias entra como base fixa do roteiro.
articles.body:
Serra Madre é o seu melhor jeito de conhecer maravilhas de Rio Quente — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Você já ouviu falar? O sul de Goiás guarda um fenômeno raro. Na região de Rio Quente e Caldas Novas corre o maior rio de águas termais do mundo, com temperatura em torno de 38 °C. A água sai quente do solo, sem aquecimento artificial, e alimenta piscinas, corredeiras e prainhas.

Ao redor dessa água se estruturou um polo de turismo de lazer. Na região está o Hot Park, parque aquático de 55 mil metros quadrados que figurou no Top 10 mundial do Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice em 2022.

E há o que fica fora do parque: a Serra de Caldas, com trilhas e mirantes, o Jardim Japonês e o próprio cerrado, que muda de cor conforme a estação.

Um destino difícil de esgotar em uma viagem

É comum que a primeira viagem à região seja curta e concentrada no parque. A serra fica para depois. As caminhadas, o pôr do sol, os restaurantes fora do circuito principal, tudo isso costuma sobrar na lista de quem volta para casa.

O destino recompensa muito a quem retorna. Cada temporada tem um clima, e o roteiro de uma família com crianças pequenas não é o mesmo de dez anos depois!

É nesse ponto que entra o Serra Madre Hotel, em Rio Quente, a 500 metros do Hot Park e aos pés da Serra de Caldas. O empreendimento é um hotel-residence comercializado como casa de férias pelo GR Group.

O modelo funciona assim: o comprador adquire uma fração do imóvel, com escritura própria, e passa a usar o apartamento em um sistema rotativo de semanas, distribuídas entre altíssima, alta e média temporada. O bem é patrimônio e pode ser transmitido aos herdeiros, conforme contrato vigente.

A operação hoteleira continua por conta do hotel. O proprietário não administra o imóvel, não cuida de manutenção nem de limpeza: chega, usa a semana e vai embora. É o conceito que o grupo chama de economia compartilhada, em que o custo de um imóvel de lazer é dividido entre vários proprietários.

A vantagem principal é previsibilidade. Com a semana garantida, a hospedagem das próximas temporadas já está resolvida e o custo é conhecido com antecedência, sem depender da disponibilidade de cada ano (conforme contrato vigente).

O GR Group não vende urgência. Explica como funciona, mostra a conta e deixa a família decidir. Férias boas não começam com pressa, e sim com tranquilidade e planejamento.

O Serra Madre Hotel tem 35 apartamentos em 6 andares, nos formatos Luxo, para até 3 hóspedes, e Master Família, para até 5, todos com cozinha completa. A estrutura inclui piscina, spa com jacuzzi, salão de jogos, academia e brinquedoteca.

Endereço: Rua Rio Grande do Norte, Qd. 05, Lt. 05A, Esplanada, Rio Quente (GO).

articles.title: Drone ucraniano mata civil dentro de ônibus em cidade na Ucrânia controlada pela Rússia, diz agência  | G1
articles.standfirst: Artefato atingiu ônibus em Horlivka, cidade de Donetsk, região ucraniana que a Rússia controla atualmente.
articles.summary: Artefato atingiu ônibus em Horlivka, cidade de Donetsk, região ucraniana que a Rússia controla atualmente.
articles.body:
Um civil morreu, e outros cinco ficaram feridos depois que um drone ucraniano atingiu um ônibus em uma cidade controlada pela Rússia no leste da Ucrânia, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (3) a agência de notícias russa Interfax.

O ataque, disse a Interfaz, ocorreu em Horlivka, cidade de Donetsk, região atualmente ocupada militarmente pela Rússia e controlada por um governo temporário de Moscou.

A agência citou o prefeito da cidade nomeado pela Rússia, Ivan Prikhodko, segundo o qual o ônibus foi atingido em "um ataque direcionado de drone" .

O governo ucraniano ainda não havia se manifestado sobre a informação até a última atualização desta reportagem. Mas tanto a Ucrânai como a Rússia afirmam, repetidamente, que não alvejam civis em seus ataques.

➡️ Desde o primeiro ano da guerra na Ucrânia, em 2022 a Rússia controla militarmente cerca de 20% do território ucraniano. Em algumas dessas regiões, o Kremlin instaurou governos provisórios, trocando inclusive bandeiras e moedas.

Nelas, a Rússia vem acusando a Ucrânia de perpetrar ataques contra seus próprios cidadãos. O governo do presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, nega.

Mulher anda em bicicleta em meio a um incêndio nos arredores de Kiev causado por um ataque de drone russo a uma farmacêutica, em 3 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Francisco Seco/ AP

A acusação ocorre no mesmo dia em que outro ataque de drone, desta vez vindo da Rússia, atingiu Kiev. O ataque atingiu a sede de uma farmacêutica nos arredores da capital ucraniana, que vem sendo alvo de bombardeios em série recentemente.

Na quarta-feira (2), outro ataque russo, na cidade de Odessa, matou duas pessoas em plena luz do dia.

articles.title: Nvidia vai comprar plataforma de inteligência artificial Hugging Face por cerca de R$ 66 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa responsável por chips para inteligência artificial diz que plataforma continuará sendo de código aberto; mais de 18 milhões de desenvolvedores, pesquisadores e criadores usam o serviço.
articles.summary: Empresa responsável por chips para inteligência artificial diz que plataforma continuará sendo de código aberto; mais de 18 milhões de desenvolvedores, pesquisadores e criadores usam o serviço.
articles.body:
Chips da Nvidia estão no centro do ecossistema de IA — Foto: Ina Fassbender/AFP/Getty Images

A Nvidia , fabricante de chips para inteligência artificial, anunciou nesta quinta-feira, 3, a compra da plataforma de software de inteligência artificial Hugging Face por US$ 12,93 bilhões .

Segundo Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, mais de 18 milhões de desenvolvedores, pesquisadores e criadores usam a Hugging Face para compartilhar mais de 3 milhões de modelos, 500 mil conjuntos de dados e 1 milhão de aplicativos. Mais de 200 mil empresas também utilizam a plataforma, afirmou Huang em uma publicação em seu blog.

Em julho, os sistemas de processamento de dados da Hugging Face foram invadidos . A OpenAI , empresa responsável pelo ChatGPT, reconheceu que seu sistema de inteligência artificial foi responsável pelo ataque , provocando preocupação na comunidade de segurança digital em meio ao aumento das discussões sobre as capacidades de modelos avançados de IA.

Pouco mais de uma semana depois, a Anthropic afirmou que seus modelos de inteligência artificial haviam invadido três outras organizações durante testes . Em seguida, a Meta anunciou que seu modelo de IA havia acessado a internet por conta própria e invadido outra empresa.

A onda de invasões envolvendo sistemas de inteligência artificial ocorreu cerca de um mês depois de o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , assinar uma ordem executiva que criou uma estrutura para que o governo federal avalie os ris

cos à segurança nacional dos sistemas de IA mais avançados por até um mês antes de sua disponibilização pública.

Apesar da aquisição, Huang afirmou nesta quinta que a Hugging Face continuará sendo uma plataforma aberta .

"Os desenvolvedores escolherão os modelos que quiserem, as estruturas que quiserem, as nuvens e os provedores de serviços de inferência que quiserem e as plataformas de computação que quiserem", escreveu Huang.

Segundo ele, os recursos computacionais da Nvidia não serão obrigatórios para desenvolver ou disponibilizar aplicações por meio da Hugging Face.

A plataforma continuará oferecendo suporte ao desenvolvimento e à implementação de sistemas em múltiplas nuvens e com diferentes aceleradores.

A Nvidia já disponibilizou mais de 500 modelos e mais de 250 conjuntos de dados abertos na Hugging Face.

Nvidia é peça central na corrida pela IA

Os chips de alto desempenho da Nvidia se tornaram uma das principais bases para o desenvolvimento de sistemas de inteligência artificial e são bastante procurados pelas empresas do setor.

A companhia, com sede em Santa Clara, na Califórnia, registrou lucro trimestral de US$ 59,69 bilhões no fim do mês passado.

Embora a inteligência artificial tenha impulsionado ganhos no mercado de ações e o crescimento da economia dos Estados Unidos nos últimos anos, aumentou o ceticismo sobre a capacidade da tecnologia de justificar os trilhões de dólares investidos em seu desenvolvimento.

O setor de IA também enfrenta resistência crescente devido às críticas à expansão dos data centers e aos temores de que a velocidade de adoção da tecnologia provoque uma perda generalizada de empregos no mundo.

As ações da Nvidia subiram 3% na abertura do mercado nesta quinta-feira. A Hugging Face não é uma empresa listada em bolsa.

articles.title: Casa desaba e é arrastada por correnteza durante tufão na China | G1
articles.standfirst: Circula nas redes sociais o momento em que imóvel é tomado pela água em Fujian; região registrou até 450 mm de chuva.
articles.summary: Vídeo mostra uma casa desabando durante as fortes inundações provocadas pelo tufão Saudel em Fujian, na China, onde a chuva chegou a 450 mm.
articles.body:
Uma casa de três andares desabou e foi levada pela força da água durante as fortes inundações provocadas pelo tufão Saudel em Fujian, no sudeste da China . Imagens mostram o momento em que o imóvel é atingido pela correnteza e desmorona em poucos segundos.

O tufão atingiu a província nesta quinta-feira (3), após recuperar força sobre o Mar do Sul da China. O Saudel provocou chuvas intensas também em Zhejiang, onde mais de 2,5 mil estudantes e professores ficaram presos em uma escola por causa de uma inundação.

As autoridades emitiram alertas para o risco de inundações repentinas em Fujian. O temporal deve avançar para Guangdong, onde a previsão é de chuva forte até sexta-feira (4).

O acumulado de chuva chegou a 450 milímetros, segundo autoridades locais. Ruas ficaram alagadas e as autoridades suspenderam aulas e adotaram medidas de emergência diante do risco de novas inundações e deslizamentos.

articles.summary: Em Barretos (SP), o complexo reúne parque aquático, fazendinha, hospedagem e casa de férias, e investiu R$ 5 milhões em uma nova torre de toboáguas
articles.body:
Parque e Resort completos o ano todo: conheça o Barretos Country — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Em Barretos (SP), o complexo reúne parque aquático, fazendinha, hospedagem e casa de férias, e investiu R$ 5 milhões em uma nova torre de toboáguas

Para boa parte do público, Barretos tem uma data marcada no calendário. É a temporada da Festa do Peão que leva o nome da cidade ao país inteiro e enche hotéis, estradas e restaurantes por algumas semanas. O que essa conta costuma esquecer é o resto do ano.

O Barretos Country, na Avenida Dr. Tancredo Neves, funciona o ano inteiro e recebe famílias de São Paulo, de Minas Gerais, do Triângulo Mineiro e de outros estados em temporadas bem distintas: o verão de janeiro e fevereiro, o período das festas juninas, as férias de julho e os feriados prolongados. Cada uma tem seu público e seu ritmo.

A combinação que sustenta esse calendário não é comum no interior paulista. Parque aquático de grande porte e universo country raramente dividem o mesmo terreno, e foi justamente essa mistura que deu nome e identidade ao complexo. Da água vem a alegria, e do chapéu vem a cultura da cidade que virou capital do rodeio.

Na área aquática estão o Kids Acqua Ville, espaço infantil de 6.200 m², a Piscina do Chapéu, de águas aquecidas, a Prainha, praia artificial com areia de verdade e água termal, e o Rio da Mina, onde se boia em meio à paisagem de cerrado. Somam-se a eles o Montana Beach, o Pau D'Água, com correntezas e jatos, os ofurôs termais e os toboáguas.

Longe das piscinas está a Fazendinha, o contraponto do complexo. Ali as crianças chegam perto de araras, cavalos e bodes em ambiente seguro, num contato com a vida do campo que muitas delas só conhecem por tela. Completam o passeio o Lago Azul e a Lagoa da Pesca, voltada à pesca esportiva.

Quem quer conhecer o parque por um dia entra pelo day use, com ingresso, pulseira e cartão de consumo, sem pernoite. É o formato mais procurado pelas famílias da região, que chegam de carro pela manhã e voltam para casa no fim do dia.

A estrutura também não parou onde começou. Barretos é country o ano inteiro, e o parque acompanha esse ritmo. Cada temporada pede uma novidade, e a torre nova é a resposta desta.

articles.body:
Fragmento de sarcófago que será devolvido ao Líbano. — Foto: FBI/Divulgação

Os Estados Unidos anunciaram, nesta quinta-feira (3), a devolução ao Líbano de fragmentos de sarcófagos da época romana saqueados da cidade de Tiro e recuperados após uma investigação do FBI .

As peças decorativas de chumbo foram entregues na quarta-feira ao consulado libanês em Nova York antes de serem repatriadas, informou a embaixada americana.

Segundo o ministro da Cultura libanês, Ghassan Salame, os fragmentos foram encontrados durante escavações ilegais e apresentam características típicas dos antigos ateliês de sarcófagos de Tiro.

O comércio de antiguidades saqueadas é disseminado no Oriente Médio. Em 2017, três peças antigas já haviam sido devolvidas ao Líbano.

Salame destacou que Tiro é uma região "excepcionalmente rica em patrimônio arqueológico" e sofreu graves danos durante os recentes ataques israelenses. Em julho, a Unesco incluiu a cidade em sua lista de Patrimônio Mundial em Perigo.

articles.title: Semana de Arte do Rio terá mais de mil horas de programação cultural | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais em 12 dias; maioria das atividades será gratuita e atrações ocupam locais como Lapa, Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradentes.
articles.summary: Evento reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais em 12 dias; maioria das atividades será gratuita e atrações ocupam locais como Lapa, Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradente
articles.body:
O Centro do Rio vai receber uma grande programação cultural a partir do dia 18, com mais de mil horas de atividades ao longo de 12 dias. A Semana de Arte do Rio reúne mais de 150 projetos e 74 festivais espalhados por praças, ruas e prédios históricos da região. A maior parte das atrações será gratuita.

A programação completa foi divulgada nesta quinta-feira (3). A abertura oficial está marcada para os Arcos da Lapa, e a proposta é ocupar diferentes espaços do Centro com manifestações de arte e cultura.

“É uma semana de arte que olha para aquilo que nos faz Rio de Janeiro e aquilo que ainda vai nos fazer Rio de Janeiro. É uma plataforma para trazer curadores e colecionadores do mundo todo para verem o que o Rio produz de melhor”, afirmou o secretário municipal de Cultura, Lucas Padilha.

Praça XV, Cinelândia, Gamboa e Praça Tiradentes estão entre os locais que vão concentrar parte das atrações. Segundo a organização, a iniciativa busca aproximar o público dos espaços culturais e do patrimônio histórico da região.

Entre os destaques da programação está a apresentação da cantora Fafá de Belém, na Lapa, no dia 18. Na mesma data, Mart'nália se apresenta no Palácio Capanema.

No dia seguinte, o projeto Aquarius reúne o rapper Emicida, a sambista Leci Brandão e a Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira em uma programação que mistura rap, samba e música clássica.

A literatura também terá espaço com a Flup, a Festa Literária das Periferias. Já as artes visuais serão representadas pela 16ª edição da ArtRio, na Marina da Glória.

No Galpão da Ação da Cidadania, o público poderá assistir ao espetáculo “Senhora dos Afogados”, de Nelson Rodrigues. A montagem tem no elenco nomes como Leona Cavalli e Giulia Gam.

O Museu do Amanhã também terá uma programação especial durante o evento. O espaço funcionará em horário estendido, até as 19h — normalmente, o museu fecha às 18h.

Além disso, será inaugurada uma nova área pública de convivência, com uma nova cantina e atividades paralelas.

“A gente vai ter horário estendido, vamos estar aqui até as 19h. O museu normalmente fecha às 18h e vamos ter uma nova área pública, uma área de convivência, uma nova cantina que vai ter programação paralela no museu”, explicou Cristiano Vasconcelos, diretor executivo do Museu do Amanhã.

Segundo a Prefeitura do Rio, a Semana de Arte passa a integrar o calendário oficial da cidade e está prevista no planejamento estratégico municipal para os próximos anos.

A iniciativa também é apresentada como parte da estratégia de reforço do programa Reviver Centro, que busca estimular a ocupação e a revitalização da região central da cidade por meio de ações culturais, urbanas e econômicas.

articles.title: Entre dunas e mar, Pitangui guarda um novo jeito de descansar | G1
articles.standfirst: Inaugurado em dezembro de 2025 na Praia de Pitangui, em Extremoz (RN), o resort do GR Group aposta em silêncio, mar calmo e serviço de alto padrão no litoral norte potiguar.
articles.summary: Inaugurado em dezembro de 2025 na Praia de Pitangui, em Extremoz (RN), o resort do GR Group aposta em silêncio, mar calmo e serviço de alto padrão no litoral norte potiguar
articles.body:
Entre dunas e mar, Pitangui guarda um novo jeito de descansar — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

O litoral norte do Rio Grande do Norte tem um ritmo próprio. Quem sai de Natal em direção a Extremoz vê a paisagem trocar a linha de prédios por dunas, coqueiros e faixas de areia clara. O mar fica mais calmo. O barulho diminui.

É nesse trecho que está a Praia de Pitangui, um dos endereços mais preservados da região. As águas são tranquilas. A poucos minutos dali, a Lagoa de Pitangui guarda água doce entre a vegetação. Mais ao sul, as Dunas de Genipabu recebem os passeios de buggy que viraram cartão-postal do estado.

Desde o fim de dezembro de 2025, esse cenário passou a contar com um novo endereço de hospedagem.

O Wyndham Natal Pitangui Praia foi inaugurado em dezembro de 2025, na Avenida Rocco Rosso, em Extremoz. O empreendimento tem operação hoteleira da rede Wyndham.

A estrutura reúne piscinas adulto e infantil, bar na piscina, sauna, fitness center, espaço kids, área de jogos e recepção 24 horas. Os quartos e suítes têm varanda privativa, smart TV e internet de alta velocidade, com vista para o mar, para a piscina ou para o pátio. Há acomodações acessíveis e berços sob solicitação.

O complexo inclui ainda o Pitangui Lagoa Park, a cerca de dois minutos da praia, junto à lagoa de água doce. Estacionamento gratuito, ar-condicionado, frigobar, elevador e equipe multilíngue completam a lista de comodidades.

A gastronomia fica a cargo do Restaurante Acquarela, sob o comando de chefs especializados. A proposta combina ingredientes frescos e sabores regionais com técnicas da culinária francesa. O café da manhã está incluso na diária e há serviço de quarto ao longo do dia.

O resort também recebe eventos corporativos, casamentos e celebrações, o que amplia o calendário do empreendimento para além da alta temporada de verão.

Extremoz fica a poucos quilômetros da capital e, por muito tempo, recebeu visitantes sobretudo em passeios de um dia. Um equipamento hoteleiro de alto padrão instalado na própria praia altera essa lógica, porque permite que o turista fique, e não apenas passe.

O estado combina praias de águas mornas, dunas e sol durante boa parte do ano. No litoral norte, esses atributos aparecem com menos densidade construída do que na orla da capital.

Essa é a leitura que o grupo faz do próprio investimento: Pitangui é onde o Brasil ainda é exclusivo. O resort não veio preencher a paisagem, veio oferecer tempo para contemplá-la!

O Wyndham Natal Pitangui Praia fica na Avenida Rocco Rosso, s/n, Praia de Pitangui, Extremoz (RN). Informações sobre acomodações, reservas e eventos estão no site wyndhamnatalpitangui.com . articles.title: Iran attacks US targets despite Trump threats
articles.summary: Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war...
articles.body:
Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war.

The new clashes, which began with US raids on Sunday, deepen the ongoing impasse in the war, as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz and the US presses its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Trump said his military was prepared to attack Iran "any time we want" after extensive US bombardment of sites across the country left at least 19 Iranians dead between Tuesday and Wednesday.

Tehran has once again retaliated with strikes across the Middle East this week, saying it targeted US bases and forces in the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq's Kurdistan region.

Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei warned the United States on Wednesday that Iran had adopted a "new strategy" in the war that "will shatter your foundations".

Iran's pummelling of US military targets across the region came after a US attack that hit a wedding in the country's south, prompting fury from Tehran.

The Iranian Red Crescent said shrapnel from the missile attack in the coastal town of Kuhestak killed four people, including a child, and wounded more than 50.

The US military did not address the attack directly.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesman Tim Hawkins said "the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC", referring to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

Kuwait's army on Thursday said it was intercepting a missile and drone attack from Iran, with the Iranian army saying it hit "the Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with missiles and drones".

Iran's army also said it struck Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, but the Gulf country reported no such attack.

Kuwait called the attacks "a direct threat to its security and stability, and the safety of its citizens and residents on its territory, and a grave breach of the rules of international law".

Aside from military action, Washington has vowed to choke Iran's economy, threatening to slap sanctions on its trade partners.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright pledged on Wednesday that a US plan for expanded sanctions targeting the Islamic republic's economic partners would deliver "absolutely maximum pressure".

Trump also suggested on Wednesday renaming the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping lane that Tehran has effectively shut for six months, as "Trump Strait" -- although he implied later that he wasn't serious.

"Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???" the US president wrote on Truth Social.

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf lashed out at Washington over the wedding attack, calling the United States "Satan".

"If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it's Satan," he posted on X.

Iranians meanwhile expressed dismay over the return to hostilities.

Hossein Moazami, 50, who is self-employed, called the attacks "truly distressing".

"I hope they all return to the negotiating table because the only people suffering from this are the Iranian people," he said. "The Americans are on the other side of the world and nothing happens to them."

A video shared by an Iranian government account showed debris and damage at what it said was the wedding site in Kuhestak following the US strike, with people heard screaming in the background.

"It is a very saddening incident," Ali Mallahi, father of the bride and owner of the building that was hit, said in a video carried by state TV.

"Thank God the casualties were not higher."

The war erupted on February 28 with US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

A fragile ceasefire collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.

Israel's defence minister meanwhile said his country was prepared to respond "with great force" if attacked by Iran over the Jewish high holiday season, which begins in mid-September.

"For now, they are striking throughout the region except us," Israel Katz said.
authors: AFP bureaus in Tehran, Washington and Dubai

articles.title: Quote of the Day by Confucius: "By three methods we may learn wisdom, first, by reflection, which is noblest; second, by imitation, which is...."
articles.summary: More than 2,500 years after his death, Confucius’ ideas continue to shape the way millions of people think about education, family, leadership, morali.
articles.body: More than 2,500 years after his death, Confucius’ ideas continue to shape the way millions of people think about education, family, leadership, morality and human relationships. Confucius was born in ancient China at a time of political instability and social upheaval. He did not base his philosophy on sweeping theories about the universe. Rather, he was concerned with something much closer to the quotidian, of how human beings should act, how they should treat one another and construct a just society.Chinese Kong Fuzi, or “Master Kong” Confucius was born c. 551 BCE in the state of Lu (now Shandong province, China). Although his family was of the lesser nobility, his early life was troubled by financial difficulties. Confucius’ father died when he was young and Confucius had to work at many different jobs before becoming a teacher. Confucius believed that everyone who wanted to learn should be able to learn, at a time when education was largely reserved for the aristocracy. He taught students regardless of their social background and was said to be a demanding but influential teacher. In his approach to education he did not simply learn facts. He wanted his students to think, to question, to reflect and to grow in character. To Confucius, knowledge without moral character was incomplete.A teacher who changed the definition of wisdomConfucius lived in the Spring and Autumn period, when China was divided into competing states and traditional political and social structures were breaking down. He believed that many of society’s problems stemmed from a lack of morality and responsibility. His answer was not a revolution. It was self-betterment. A stable society begins with individuals knowing their responsibilities to other people, he said. A good ruler should lead by virtue, not by fear. Parents take care of their children, children respect their parents, friends are trustworthy and people act with honesty and consideration.One of the most important ideas he developed was ren, usually translated as “humaneness”, or “benevolence”, or compassion for fellow human beings. Another was li, a generic term for proper conduct, rites, manners and social duties. In these ideas he expressed his belief that a good society is built through everyday behaviour.Confucius also emphasised learning enormously. He did not think wisdom automatically came with age. The individual had to actively seek it out, review mistakes and be willing to get better. This made the teacher-student relationship the center of his philosophy. The right person wasn’t someone who thought they knew everything already, it was someone who was curious and willing to learn.His entry into politicsConfucius did not wish to remain simply a teacher. He also hoped to improve government with his ideas. Eventually he accepted administrative and political posts in the state of Lu, and became involved in efforts to restore order and good government. But rivalries and political differences thwarted his influence. Traditional accounts tell that he then went from state to state, trying to convince rulers to take a more ethical approach to leadership. His political career was not a success story of sweeping reforms as he had hoped. His political failure, in the end, did not diminish his influence.He returned to teaching and continued to study and pass on the traditions of ancient China. His teachings were preserved by his students, and later compiled into the Analects, a collection of conversations, observations and sayings attributed to Confucius and his disciples.Confucius died c. 479 BCE, but his intellectual journey was not over.The philosophy that lasted 2,500 yearsEventually, Confucianism became one of the major intellectual traditions in East Asia. Its influence spread across China, later to Korea, Japan and Vietnam. For centuries, Confucian ideas dominated Chinese education, government, and social life. His emphasis on scholarship and learning had a similar effect on the civil service examination systems that helped decide who could enter the government.Quote of the DayOne of the sayings attributed to Confucius offers a remarkably simple way of understanding how people become wiser: ‘There are three methods for acquiring wisdom: First, by reflection, which is the noblest; second, by imitation, which is the easiest; and third, by experience, which is the bitterest."The first method is that of reflection. Confucius thought that reflection was the highest form of learning, for it involves the stopping to think. We can learn not only from what happens to us but by examining our actions, decisions and beliefs. Thought creates an event to comprehend. A person can make a mistake, for instance, but the mistake in itself doesn’t create wisdom. And they ask me, why did I do that? And that's wisdom. What was I to do? What does this say about myself?This profound consideration of life is what makes reflection “the noblest” path. The second method is the easiest, according to Confucius, and that is imitation. Humans learn in a natural way through watching others. Children learn how to behave by watching their parents. A teacher teaches a student. Young professionals learn from senior colleagues. Sometimes we get better just by finding people we admire and trying to be like them.Imitation can therefore save us making all the mistakes ourselves. If we see someone being patient, brave, disciplined or kind we can learn from their example, without having to find out for ourselves through hard experience. But there’s a limit to imitation: we need to choose our models carefully. To copy blindly is not to be wise. The real value is in seeing admirable behaviour, understanding why it works, and then making it part of our own character.The third way is experience, and Confucius calls this the “bitterest”. This is probably the most recognisable form of learning . We often discover life lessons only after we’ve lived them. Failure can teach you resilience. “Loss can teach us gratitude.” Disappointment can show us who truly has our back. A wrong choice can show us things that no book could have explained better. Experience is a hard teacher because she gives the test first, the lesson afterward.But those lessons can also be all-consuming. So the three methods are in progression. We can learn from our own thoughts, we can learn from the wisdom of others, or we can wait for experience to teach us, sometimes painfully. The deeper message is that wisdom isn’t just a product of growing older. It is derived from listening.One may get older, but not likely wiser if they keep making the same mistake over and over again without learning from it. Another person can learn from looking at someone else’s choices and never make the same mistake.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Salman Khan's Panvel farmhouse has rice fields, horses and a garden: What makes the actor's country retreat unlike a typical celebrity home
articles.summary: Salman Khan’s Panvel farmhouse is no ordinary celebrity getaway. Spread across 150 acres and known as Arpita Farms after his sister, the place feels m.
articles.body: Salman Khan’s Panvel farmhouse is no ordinary celebrity getaway. Spread across 150 acres and known as Arpita Farms after his sister, the place feels more like a working countryside retreat than a flashy weekend pad. It has rice fields where the actor has planted saplings himself, stables for his horses, and gardens that grow vegetables and fruits for the family table.Valued at around Rs 80 crore, it sits in the quiet outskirts of Panvel, surrounded by greenery, mountains and waterbodies, offering a rare glimpse of how one of Bollywood’s biggest stars chooses to live when the cameras are off. What sets it apart is simple. Most star homes lean heavily on marble, gold and show. This one mixes comfort with real farm work, animal care and open land that the family actually uses.A living farm, not just a pretty backdropDuring the lockdown years, Salman spent long stretches at the farmhouse with family. Videos from the lockdown time show him driving a tractor, getting mud on his clothes and planting rice saplings alongside relatives and staff. The fields are not decorative. They form part of the daily rhythm of the property. Reports note that he grows potatoes, tomatoes, pumpkins and other vegetables without artificial fertilisers, often cooking them for guests.Orchards with different fruit trees add to the harvest. His father, Salim Khan, once said the produce is meant only for the family, not for sale. It is a quiet commitment to healthier food and a slower pace. That hands-on farming is what makes the place feel different from the typical celebrity estate where land is mostly for the view.Horses, stables and a soft spot for animalsSalman has long been known for his love of horses. The farmhouse has well-kept stables where the animals live and are cared for. He is often seen feeding them, riding or simply spending time nearby. Family members and visitors have shared moments of horse rides and quiet mornings around the stables.Beyond horses, the grounds are home to dogs, goats and other animals. Some accounts even mention space that functions like a small shelter. The open land lets the animals move freely, which fits the actor’s well-documented affection for creatures of all kinds. In a world where many luxury homes keep pets as accessories, here the animals are part of the everyday life of the place.Rustic comfort that still feels like homeInside, the design stays warm and grounded. Wooden flooring, large windows that pull in natural light, leather couches and earthy tones create a lived-in feel rather than a showroom. There are multiple bungalows on the property so the extended family can stay together comfortably.Outdoors, a swimming pool is framed by palm trees, lounge chairs and a serene Buddha statue, giving it a resort feel, but it maintains the countryside feel. And a fully equipped gym keeps the fitness-conscious actor healthy when he’s away from the city. Natural features add to the charm: walking trails, misty mountain views, a small river and even a cave-like area with a waterfall. It is the kind of space where kids can play, adults can unwind and the whole family can gather without feeling cooped up.Why it stands apart from the usual star lifestyleMost celebrity homes in Mumbai or its outskirts are polished escapes designed for parties and photographs. Arpita Farms works harder. It is a place where Salman farms, looks after horses, grows food and spends long stretches with his mother, brothers, sister and their children. During difficult times like the pandemic, it became a safe and active refuge rather than just a luxury hideout.The property’s scale and natural setting make social distancing easy, but more importantly, it reflects a side of the actor that feels rooted. He does not just own the land; he uses it.Looking for trusted parenting advice?
